Question: Which of the four methods (ResNet, DANN, CDAN-f, CDAN-fg) is most effective at separating the two classes of data points?
Evidence:
[E1] (figure, Figure 3, page 9) (image attached): Figure 3: T-SNE of (a) ResNet, (b) DANN, (c) CDAN- f , (d) CDAN- fg (red: A ; blue: W ).
Words printed in the figure: which is slightly more costly than CDAN (RM), while CDAN (RM) has similar cost as DA (a) ResNet (b) DANN (c) CDAN-f (d) CDAN-fg
[E2] (figure, Figure 3, page 9): a zoomed view of Figure 3 (image attached) [image]

claims.text: Figure 3 shows T-SNE visualizations for (a) ResNet, (b) DANN, (c) CDAN- f , and (d) CDAN- fg with red representing class A and blue representing class W.

cites.quote: Figure 3: T-SNE of (a) ResNet, (b) DANN, (c) CDAN- f , (d) CDAN- fg (red: A ; blue: W ).

claims.text: Among the four methods shown, CDAN-fg is the most effective at separating the two classes of data points, as it forms distinct, well-separated clusters where the red and blue data points are grouped closely together within separate localized structures.

cites.observation: CDAN-fg shows multiple distinct, well-separated clusters containing tight groups of red and blue data points.
